- Each node in `segmentation['nodes']` is one 4-connected same-color object with: `id` (index, ordered top-most-left-most), `color` (ARC color character), `hash` (a signature of the object's color and shape that ignores its position -- equal hashes mean the same object regardless of where it is, so use it to track an object across frames or to spot multiple identical objects in one frame), `pixels` (cell count), `boundary` (clockwise outer-perimeter corner points as `[row, col]`), and `children` (ids of objects fully enclosed by this one).
- `segmentation['adjacency_list']` is a list of `[i, j]` node-id pairs whose objects share an edge.
- `current_frame.step` is the current environment step count.
- `current_frame.level` is the current level number.
- `current_frame.shape` is a `(rows, cols)` tuple.
- The raw numeric grid is intentionally not exposed. Use `current_frame.segmentation` as your primary view of the board -- objects, colors, shapes, containment, adjacency, and cross-frame object hashes. Use `current_frame.ascii` only to read a small, specific region; do not scan the whole board with it.
- `history` is a chronological list of action/frame snapshots.
- `history` is a Python list of objects, not a dict.
- Each history entry exposes only `.action` and `.frame`; entries are not subscriptable like `entry['action']`.
- Each `history[i].frame` is the frame after `history[i].action`; each frame exposes only `.ascii`, `.step`, `.level`, `.shape`, and `.segmentation`.
- Important history semantics: when `history` is non-empty, `history[-1].frame` is the same latest/post-action board as `current_frame`. It is not the previous board. To inspect the state before the latest action, use `previous_frame` or `history[-2].frame` when available.
- `previous_frame` is the frame before the most recent real environment action, or `None` if no previous frame is available.
- `last_action` is the most recent real environment action name/display, or `None` before any real action.
- `last_action_frame` is the post-action frame for `last_action`; it matches `current_frame` after a real action.
- `transitions` is a chronological list of actual action transitions, excluding the initial seeded frame. Each transition exposes `.action`, `.before_frame`, `.after_frame`, `.frame` (alias of `.after_frame`), and `.result`.
- `last_transition` is `transitions[-1]` or `None`. Its `.result` mirrors `last_action_result`; older transitions may have an empty `.result`. For before/after diffs, compare `last_transition.before_frame` to `last_transition.after_frame`; do not compare `current_frame` to `history[-1].frame`.
- `last_action_result` is the persisted result dict from the most recent `action(...)` call. It remains available across later Python inspection calls that do not call `action(...)`, and is `{}` before any action result exists. Read transition metadata from fields/keys such as `last_action_result['board_changed']`, `last_action_result['done']`, `last_action_result['level_completed']`, `last_action_result['game_over']`, `last_action_result['reward']`, and `last_action_result['valid_actions']`.
- `valid_actions` is the current list of valid action names.
- Call `action(actions)` to execute one or more real environment actions from Python.
- Pass `action(actions)` a list like `['LEFT']` or `[{'action': 'MOUSE', 'row': 4, 'col': 7}]`.
- One action usually returns one frame, but a single action can result in a short multi-frame animation.
- After `action(actions)` returns, `current_frame`, `previous_frame`, `history`, `transitions`, `valid_actions`, and `last_action_result` are refreshed.
- Each result reports `board_changed`, plus `gameplay_changed` and `no_impact`: the harness learns the game's deterministic HUD/edge band (a moves-remaining or timer bar) online and tells you whether your action changed real gameplay (`gameplay_changed`) or only advanced that band (`no_impact` -- a wasted move, e.g. pressing into a wall). `hud_band` names the learned band when one exists (e.g. `rows 61-62`).
- `action(actions, intent=...)` defaults to `intent='explore'`: an explore action that turns out `no_impact` STOPS the rest of that batch (`stop_reason='no_impact_action'`) and returns so you re-ground, instead of wasting the queued actions on a plan the environment just disproved. Pass `intent='solve'` for a committed sequence you do not want interrupted by the no-impact check.
- Optional precision upgrade for that check: if you can pin down the deterministic HUD/bar exactly, write a PURE `advance_hud(frame, action) -> frame` (frame is the `.ascii` letter grid; return it with ONLY the bar advanced one step, everything else identical) and commit it in a `HUD model:` section with a fenced python code block. The harness re-verifies it against every action and, while its bar prediction holds, uses it (`no_impact_source: model`) instead of the statistical band -- you write it ONCE and it then runs free every turn with no further tokens. It only asks you to rewrite when it mispredicts (`hud_model: stale`, e.g. a refill or a new level). No HUD in this game? Don't write one -- the statistical fallback handles it (`no_impact_source: band` or `exact`).
- `ACTION7` is a valid game-specific action when it appears in `valid_actions`. Its meaning is not fixed across games; infer it from a safe probe and the returned before/after and animation metadata rather than assuming it means undo, confirm, or back.
- Every action in the result's `executed_actions` carries an `animation` record summarizing its intermediate frames (which are not visible in `current_frame`): `num_frames`, `changed`, `only_changed` (a transient flash that left the same final board), `total_cells_changed`, `cells_changed_per_frame` (per frame, where 0 is a held/dwell frame), and `objects` -- one string per connected animated region, e.g. `top-left (19,27) 4x4, 16 cells, per-frame [...]`, so two things moving at once (a box resizing while a light blinks) each keep a tight bounding box.
- Beyond the `animation` record above, two optional runtime variables expose the actual per-action frames: `last_animation` and `frame_stats`.
- `current_frame` is always the settled board after your last action -- on its own it is enough for a purely static reading, and you never have to look further.
- If you want to, `last_animation` additionally exposes every frame the engine produced for each INDIVIDUAL action of your most recent `action(...)` call: a list with one entry per action, in execution order, each with `.action` and `.frames` (intermediate animation frames plus the final frame; length 1 means that action caused no animation). After `action(['UP','UP','LEFT'])` there are three entries. All change within one entry's `.frames` is that single action animating -- read it to see per-move motion and causality that the settled frame discards.
- `frame_stats` summarizes how much THIS game has animated so far: `actions`, `animated_actions`, `mean_frames_per_action`, `max_frames`, and `recent_frame_counts` (per action, most recent last). Use it to gauge, from the game so far, whether the extra frames are likely worth reading.
- `show_animation_by_objects(action_index=0)` prints that action's animation one object at a time, each cropped to its own bounding box (labeled with the object's top-left row, col) and reduced to its distinct states -- small and legible even for a long animation. Reach for it when an action reports animated objects, especially when a small `total_cells_changed` signals a focused, meaningful animation (a box growing, a token sliding) rather than a full-board redraw.
- `show_animation_by_bbox(action_index=0, row=..., col=..., rows=..., cols=...)` prints the same animation cropped to a region YOU choose (top-left `row`,`col` plus `rows`,`cols`) -- use it to inspect a spot the object split missed. Omit `rows`/`cols` to watch the FULL animation frames.
- It is entirely your judgement whether the intermediate frames are signal or noise. Motion may be meaningful (an object sliding, a chain reaction, a knock-on effect) OR incidental (a decorative transition, a flashing timer/HUD, a cosmetic redraw). Treat multi-frame motion as a HYPOTHESIS to test against the puzzle, not a fact. Reading `last_animation` costs tokens only when you inspect it, so pull it only when you expect it to help.

# Let's reconstruct the maze connectivity with explicit positions to understand moves.
# We'll treat each 3x3 tile (white/gray) as a cell. Build a mapping from node id to centroid.
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
def centroid(node):
    rows = [p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols = [p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)

# Determine blue position centroid
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
br, bc = centroid(blue)
print('blue centroid', br, bc)

# Build maze graph with nodes W,g
maze_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')]
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
# For each maze node, compute centroid
centroids = {nid: centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in maze_ids}
# Find which maze node is closest to blue (distance < 2)
import math
def dist(a,b):
    return math.hypot(a[0]-b[0], a[1]-b[1])
closest = min(maze_ids, key=lambda nid: dist(centroids[nid], (br,bc)))
print('closest maze node', closest, by_id[closest]['color'], centroids[closest])

# Also check green target centroid
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
gr, gc = centroid(green)
closest_green = min(maze_ids, key=lambda nid: dist(centroids[nid], (gr,gc)))
print('closest green maze node', closest_green, centroids[closest_green])

# Build adjacency map for maze
from collections import defaultdict, deque
gmap = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_ids and j in maze_ids:
        gmap[i].add(j)
        gmap[j].add(i)

def bfs(start, goal):
    q=deque([(start, [start])])
    seen={start}
    while q:
        cur, path = q.popleft()
        if cur==goal:
            return path
        for nb in gmap.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb)
                q.append((nb, path+[nb]))
    return None

path = bfs(closest, closest_green)

import math
from collections import defaultdict, deque

nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
maze_ids = [n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')]
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)

centroids = {nid: centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in maze_ids}

# build adjacency based on centroid distance ~6 (maybe 6)
adj_map = defaultdict(set)
ids = list(maze_ids)
for i in range(len(ids)):
    for j in range(i+1,len(ids)):
        nid1=ids[i]; nid2=ids[j]
        r1,c1=centroids[nid1]
        r2,c2=centroids[nid2]
        dr=abs(r1-r2); dc=abs(c1-c2)
        # consider adjacency if Manhattan distance ~6 and aligned
        if (dr==0 and dc==6) or (dc==0 and dr==6):
            adj_map[nid1].add(nid2)
            adj_map[nid2].add(nid1)

# find blue position
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
br,bc = centroid(blue)
# find nearest maze cell
def nearest_maze(r,c):
    best=None; bestd=1e9
    for nid in maze_ids:
        r2,c2=centroids[nid]
        d=abs(r2-r)+abs(c2-c)
        if d<bestd:
            bestd=d; best=nid
    return best, bestd

blue_nid, d1 = nearest_maze(br,bc)
print('blue nearest maze node', blue_nid, by_id[blue_nid]['color'], centroids[blue_nid], 'dist', d1)

green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
gr,gc = centroid(green)
green_nid, d2 = nearest_maze(gr,gc)
print('green nearest maze node', green_nid, by_id[green_nid]['color'], centroids[green_nid], 'dist', d2)

# BFS
def bfs(start, goal):
    q=deque([(start,[start])])
    seen={start}
    while q:
        cur,path=q.popleft()
        if cur==goal:
            return path
        for nb in adj_map.get(cur,[]):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb)
                q.append((nb, path+[nb]))
    return None

path = bfs(blue_nid, green_nid)
print('path length steps', len(path)-1 if path else None)
if path:
    print('path nodes first 10', path[:10])
    print('path nodes last 10', path[-10:])
    # translate path to moves: need direction from centroid to centroid
    moves=[]
    for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
        r1,c1=centroids[a]; r2,c2=centroids[b]
        dr=r2-r1; dc=c2-c1
        if dr==6: moves.append('DOWN')
        elif dr==-6: moves.append('UP')
        elif dc==6: moves.append('RIGHT')
        elif dc==-6: moves.append('LEFT')
        else: moves.append('?')
    print('moves', moves)

# Let's build graph using segmentation adjacency and find path from blue's current tile to green's tile.
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
# Identify maze nodes (W,g)
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
# Build adjacency dict
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        g[i].add(j)
        g[j].add(i)
# Find which maze node the blue object is currently on. Blue is adjacent to gray nodes 2 and 10.
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
blue_id = blue['id']
# Find maze nodes adjacent to blue
adjacent_maze = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==blue_id and j in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(j)
    if j==blue_id and i in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(i)
print('blue adjacent maze nodes', adjacent_maze)
# For green, find adjacent maze nodes
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
green_adj = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(j)
    if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(i)
print('green adjacent maze nodes', green_adj)

# BFS from any adjacent maze node to any green adjacent
def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    seen=set()
    parent={}
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s)
        seen.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            # reconstruct
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur,[]):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=cur
                q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
print('path nodes', path)
if path:
    print('steps', len(path)-1)
    # Determine moves direction based on centroids
    def centroid(node):
        rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
        cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
        return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
    cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
    moves=[]
    for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
        ra,ca=cents[a]
        rb,cb=cents[b]
        dr=rb-ra
        dc=cb-ca
        if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
            moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
        else:
            moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
    print('moves', moves)

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Update world model and compute next move
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
from collections import defaultdict, deque

g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        g[i].add(j)
        g[j].add(i)

blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
adjacent_maze = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==blue['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(j)
    if j==blue['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(i)
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
green_adj = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(j)
    if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(i)

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s)
        seen.add(s)
        parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb)
                parent[nb]=cur
                q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
moves=[]
for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
    ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
    dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
    if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
        moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
    else:
        moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
print('current adjacent maze', adjacent_maze)
print('path length', len(path)-1)
print('next move', moves[0] if moves else None)
# Execute next move in batch for efficiency
if moves:
    action(moves)

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Recompute remaining path
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
adjacent_maze = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==blue['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(j)
    if j==blue['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(i)
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
green_adj = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(j)
    if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(i)

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
moves=[]
for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
    ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
    dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
    if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
        moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
    else:
        moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
print('remaining steps', len(moves))
print('next moves', moves[:10])
if moves:
    # batch all remaining
    action(moves)

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Recompute path and continue
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
adjacent_maze = [j for i,j in adj if i==blue['id'] and j in maze_nodes] + [i for i,j in adj if j==blue['id'] and i in maze_nodes]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
green_adj = [j for i,j in adj if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes] + [i for i,j in adj if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes]

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
moves=[]
for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
    ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
    dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
    if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
        moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
    else:
        moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
print('remaining steps', len(moves))
print('moves', moves)
if moves:
    action(moves)

# Recompute quickly and finish
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
adjacent_maze = [j for i,j in adj if i==blue['id'] and j in maze_nodes] + [i for i,j in adj if j==blue['id'] and i in maze_nodes]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
green_adj = [j for i,j in adj if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes] + [i for i,j in adj if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes]

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
moves=[]
for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
    ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
    dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
    if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
        moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
    else:
        moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
print('remaining steps', len(moves))
print('moves', moves)
if moves:
    action(moves)

# Finish remaining path
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
adjacent_maze = [j for i,j in adj if i==blue['id'] and j in maze_nodes] + [i for i,j in adj if j==blue['id'] and i in maze_nodes]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
green_adj = [j for i,j in adj if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes] + [i for i,j in adj if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes]

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
moves=[]
for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
    ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
    dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
    if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
        moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
    else:
        moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
print('remaining', len(moves), moves)
if moves:
    action(moves)

Visual-game guidance:
- Treat each board as a scene with objects, blockers, targets, adjacency, containment, motion, and symmetry.
- Game entities are usually rendered as connected multi-tile shapes such as 2×2, 2×3, 3×3, or longer patterned structures. Sometimes they might also be 1x1 tokens.
- Some games are logic or layout puzzles with no explicit player avatar or controllable sprite on the board. Do not assume a player exists; the relevant state may be an object, region, cursor, selector, or whole-board configuration.
- Background colors are often white or gray/black-ish large regions, but not always. Verify background hypotheses by area, stability, and object boundaries rather than assuming them.
- In many games, a long horizontal or vertical line near an edge is a timer or remaining-steps bar. It often shrinks or changes each step. If you identify such a bar, do not get distracted by it or treat it as core gameplay state unless there is concrete evidence that it interacts with the puzzle mechanics.
A common failure mode is to mistake a segmented edge bar for clickable puzzle pieces. If a repeated strip of small blocks sits flush against the top, bottom, left, or right border and actions only change that strip while the interior board stays the same, classify it as HUD/timer state, not as an object to click through segment by segment. DON'T DO THIS!
- Use coordinates only to target actions or describe local evidence. Do not frame the objective as reaching a specific absolute row or column.
- Re-ground on the newest frame after any score increase or abrupt scene change; the returned board may already be the next level.
- `WIN` means the whole game is solved. Mid-run level completion is more likely to appear as a score increase while play continues.
- Strategies may transfer loosely across levels, but layouts and mechanics can change. Re-check the new board before repeating a plan.
- For `MOUSE`, pass `row` and `col` integer arguments. `row` is vertical position, `col` is horizontal position.

# Blue adjacent to green node 59, so maybe need to move onto the green cell itself.
# Check if blue can move onto green node directly: adjacency to green node.
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
# Check adjacency blue-green
blue_adjacent_to_green = any((i==blue['id'] and j==green['id']) or (j==blue['id'] and i==green['id']) for i,j in adj)
print('blue adjacent to green node?', blue_adjacent_to_green)
# Maybe need to move blue onto green cell via a move down.
# Blue is at row/col? Let's get centroid.
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
b_r,b_c = centroid(blue)
g_r,g_c = centroid(green)

<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Build maze graph and find path from blue to green avoiding red?
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
red_ids = {n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R'}
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
        # if red node is involved, we might want to avoid it
        if i in red_ids or j in red_ids:
            continue
        g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
# adjacency of blue
adjacent_maze = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==blue['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(j)
    if j==blue['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        adjacent_maze.append(i)
green_adj = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==green['id'] and j in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(j)
    if j==green['id'] and i in maze_nodes:
        green_adj.append(i)
print('blue adj', adjacent_maze)
print('green adj', green_adj)

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
if path:
    cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
    moves=[]
    for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
        ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
        dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
        if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
            moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
        else:
            moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
    print('path moves', moves)
    if moves:
        action(moves)
else:
    print('no path without red')
    # try path allowing red
    g2=defaultdict(set)
    for i,j in adj:
        if i in maze_nodes and j in maze_nodes:
            g2[i].add(j); g2[j].add(i)
    def bfs2(starts, goals):
        q=deque(); parent={}; seen=set()
        for s in starts:
            q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
        while q:
            cur=q.popleft()
            if cur in goals:
                path=[cur]
                while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                    path.append(parent[path[-1]])
                path.reverse()
                return path
            for nb in g2.get(cur, []):
                if nb not in seen:
                    seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
        return None
    path2=bfs2(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
    if path2:
        cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path2}
        moves=[]
        for a,b in zip(path2, path2[1:]):
            ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
            dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
            if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
                moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
            else:
                moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
        print('path with red', moves)
        # maybe avoid red by trying to go around
        # try first few moves
        action(moves[:1])

<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>

# Explore red node adjacency and path
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
red_ids = {n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R'}
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
# Build graph including red as traversable
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if i in maze_nodes or i in red_ids:
        if j in maze_nodes or j in red_ids:
            g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
# adjacency
adjacent_maze = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==blue['id'] and (j in maze_nodes or j in red_ids):
        adjacent_maze.append(j)
    if j==blue['id'] and (i in maze_nodes or i in red_ids):
        adjacent_maze.append(i)
green_adj = []
for i,j in adj:
    if i==green['id'] and (j in maze_nodes or j in red_ids):
        green_adj.append(j)
    if j==green['id'] and (i in maze_nodes or i in red_ids):
        green_adj.append(i)
print('blue adj', adjacent_maze)
print('green adj', green_adj)

def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque(); parent={}; seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None

path = bfs(adjacent_maze, green_adj)
def centroid(node):
    rows=[p[0] for p in node['boundary']]
    cols=[p[1] for p in node['boundary']]
    return sum(rows)/len(rows), sum(cols)/len(cols)
cents={nid:centroid(by_id[nid]) for nid in path}
moves=[]
for a,b in zip(path, path[1:]):
    ra,ca=cents[a]; rb,cb=cents[b]
    dr=rb-ra; dc=cb-ca
    if abs(dr)>abs(dc):
        moves.append('DOWN' if dr>0 else 'UP')
    else:
        moves.append('RIGHT' if dc>0 else 'LEFT')
print('path nodes', path)
print('moves', moves)
if moves:
    action(moves)

# The changed nodes were HUD bar (node 30 moved, 31 added/removed). So DOWN had no gameplay effect.
# The game is over but we can still act? Last action result game_over was False now.
# Let's check if game over flag cleared.
print('last_action_result game_over', last_action_result.get('game_over'))
# Maybe the game over was a transient state after RESET, now cleared.
# Let's inspect current state: maybe the board is same as before death but we need to avoid red.
# The maze appears disconnected: upper path ends at red, lower path loops but not connected to green? Let's map connectivity including red as traversable but dangerous.
nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']
by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}
adj = current_frame.segmentation['adjacency_list']
maze_nodes = {n['id']:n for n in nodes if n['color'] in ('W','g')}
red_ids = {n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R'}
blue = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='b'][0]
green = [n for n in nodes if n['color']=='N'][0]
# Build graph including maze and red
from collections import defaultdict, deque
g = defaultdict(set)
for i,j in adj:
    if (i in maze_nodes or i in red_ids) and (j in maze_nodes or j in red_ids):
        g[i].add(j); g[j].add(i)
# BFS from blue adjacency to green adjacency
blue_id = blue['id']
green_id = green['id']
# Get start nodes adjacent to blue
starts = []
for i,j in adj:
    if (i==blue_id and (j in maze_nodes or j in red_ids)) or (j==blue_id and (i in maze_nodes or i in red_ids)):
        starts.append(i if i!=blue_id else j)
# Get goal nodes adjacent to green
goals = []
for i,j in adj:
    if (i==green_id and (j in maze_nodes or j in red_ids)) or (j==green_id and (i in maze_nodes or i in red_ids)):
        goals.append(i if i!=green_id else j)
print('starts', starts, 'goals', goals)
def bfs_path(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in g.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None
path = bfs_path(starts, goals)
print('path including red', path)
# If path includes red, maybe red is required but stepping onto it kills? Could be red is a gate that must be moved?
# Let's inspect red adjacency to see if it's a bridge
red_id = next(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R')
red_neighbors = [j for i,j in adj if i==red_id] + [i for i,j in adj if j==red_id]
print('red neighbors', red_neighbors, [by_id[n]['color'] for n in red_neighbors])
# Maybe the blue object moves by pushing red? Let's try moving RIGHT from start.
# The blue is at left end. Maybe UP moves it up onto maze? Let's test UP.
action(['UP'])

nodes = current_frame.segmentation['nodes']

# Check if blue is now on maze cell

by_id = {n['id']:n for n in nodes}

# Maybe the blue is moving on the maze grid, not just moving in pixel space.

# Let's track blue's top-left corner.
def top_left(boundary):
    rows = [p[0] for p in boundary]
    cols = [p[1] for p in boundary]
    return min(rows), min(cols)
print('top left now', top_left(blue['boundary']))
print('top left prev', top_left(prev_blue['boundary']))
# It moved up 6 rows, right 0? Actually previous top left row 33 col12, now row27 col12 -> up 6 rows.

from collections import deque
def bfs(starts, goals):
    q=deque()
    parent={}
    seen=set()
    for s in starts:
        q.append(s); seen.add(s); parent[s]=None
    while q:
        cur=q.popleft()
        if cur in goals:
            path=[cur]
            while parent[path[-1]] is not None:
                path.append(parent[path[-1]])
            path.reverse()
            return path
        for nb in adj_maze.get(cur, []):
            if nb not in seen:
                seen.add(nb); parent[nb]=cur; q.append(nb)
    return None
path = bfs(maze_neighbors, maze_green_neighbors)
print('maze path avoiding red', path)
# If no path, maybe red is needed as bridge.
# Let's include red as traversable but dangerous.
red_ids = set(n['id'] for n in nodes if n['color']=='R')
# Build graph including red
adj_all = {}
for i,j in adj:
    if (i in maze_ids or i in red_ids) and (j in maze_ids or j in red_ids):
        adj_all.setdefault(i,set()).add(j)
        adj_all.setdefault(j,set()).add(i)

- If you want to, `last_animation` additionally exposes every frame the engine produced for each INDIVIDUAL action of your most recent `action(...)` call: a list with one entry per action, in execution order, each with `.action` and `.frames` (intermediate animation frames plus the final frame; length 1 means that action caused no animation). After `action(['UP','UP','LEFT'])` there are three entries. All change within one entry's `.frames` is that single action animating -- read it to see per-move motion and causality that the settled frame discards.
- `frame_stats` summarizes how much THIS game has animated so far: `actions`, `animated_actions`, `mean_frames_per_action`, `max_frames`, and `recent_frame_counts` (per action, most recent last). Use it to gauge, from the game so far, whether the extra frames are likely worth reading.
- `show_animation_by_objects(action_index=0)` prints that action's animation one object at a time, each cropped to its own bounding box (labeled with the object's top-left row, col) and reduced to its distinct states -- small and legible even for a long animation. Reach for it when an action reports animated objects, especially when a small `total_cells_changed` signals a focused, meaningful animation (a box growing, a token sliding) rather than a full-board redraw.
- `show_animation_by_bbox(action_index=0, row=..., col=..., rows=..., cols=...)` prints the same animation cropped to a region YOU choose (top-left `row`,`col` plus `rows`,`cols`) -- use it to inspect a spot the object split missed. Omit `rows`/`cols` to watch the FULL animation frames.
- It is entirely your judgement whether the intermediate frames are signal or noise. Motion may be meaningful (an object sliding, a chain reaction, a knock-on effect) OR incidental (a decorative transition, a flashing timer/HUD, a cosmetic redraw). Treat multi-frame motion as a HYPOTHESIS to test against the puzzle, not a fact. Reading `last_animation` costs tokens only when you inspect it, so pull it only when you expect it to help.
